title: The Broken Map of Rome
logline: A newly found piece of Rome's ancient marble map vanishes before its show. A mysterious Owl leaves cards across Rome, and the trail leads from a plaster copy to a builder who wants an old Roman library buried under concrete.

coreMystery.question: Who took the new piece of Rome's marble map, and why?
coreMystery.truth: On Tuesday, the builder Bruno Valli borrowed the piece 'for poster photos' and had a mould made at the Bassi workshop. On Thursday at 7 PM he picked up the plaster copy; at 11 PM he 'checked the lights' and swapped it into the glass case; at 11:50 PM the real piece reached his site at Piazza della Civetta. On Friday, restorer Livia Conti saw the piece was a copy. Nobody believed her, so at midnight she turned the lights off, carried the copy out, and left owl cards to lead the detective to the proof.
coreMystery.culprit: Bruno Valli, sponsor of the show and owner of Valli Building.
coreMystery.motive: The piece shows an old Roman library under Piazza della Civetta, where his company is about to pour concrete for a car park. If people saw it, the city would stop the work and he would lose his money.
coreMystery.method: A borrowed piece, a plaster copy made from a mould, a swap at night while 'checking the lights', the real piece hidden in his site's box room.

themes: Evidence over guesses: every suspect is cleared or caught by something written down.
Speaking up when nobody listens (Livia), and listening better (Sofia).
Wisdom over wealth: the owl's SAPIENTIA against Valli's money.
A city's history lives under its streets.
startingSituation: Saturday morning at the Capitoline Museums: the glass case for a newly found piece of the marble map is empty. The night guard heard nothing; the hall went dark for ten minutes at midnight. An owl card at the back door says the piece is not lost.
ending: The real piece is back in its case with Livia's name beside it. The library under Piazza della Civetta is saved and will become a small museum. Valli must answer to the city. Livia's seven gold tiles spell HISTORY.

characters.name: Giulia Marino
characters.role: Museum guide and the detective's partner
characters.personality: Warm, quick, loves maps and Italian words; says what she feels.
characters.purpose: The player's companion: explains Rome, carries the Italian word list, keeps the team moving.
characters.appearance: Late twenties, short dark curly hair, round glasses, a mustard-yellow scarf, a canvas guide's bag with folded maps.

relationships.relation: Her friend and colleague; she never guessed Livia was the Owl.

characters.name: Sofia Ferri
characters.personality: Proud, careful, under pressure from the show's sponsor; fair once she sees proof.
characters.purpose: Opens the case; her disbelief is why Livia had to act alone; she brings the inspector in Act 3.
characters.appearance: Fifties, silver bob, navy suit, a small gold brooch, reading glasses on a chain.

relationships.relation: Did not believe Livia on Friday; apologises in Case 11.
Trusted him as the show's sponsor.

characters.name: Enzo Greco
characters.role: Night guard of the map hall
characters.personality: Gentle, a little sleepy, honest; writes everything in his log.
characters.purpose: His Friday log sets the dark ten minutes; his word about Thursday's 'lights check' traps Valli.
characters.appearance: Sixties, grey moustache, guard's cap and jacket, a thermos of coffee.

relationships.relation: Let him in on Thursday night to 'check the lights'.

characters.name: Livia Conti
characters.role: Young stone restorer, secretly the Owl
characters.personality: Quiet, precise, brave in her own way; loves puzzles and owls.
characters.purpose: The season's hidden helper: she saw the copy, took it out and left the owl trail; revealed in Case 08.
characters.appearance: Mid twenties, long brown braid, white lab coat over a green jumper, a silver owl ring; in Case 08 a grey hooded coat.

relationships.relation: Her director, who did not believe her.
Heard from him about Thursday's 'lights check'.

characters.name: Bruno Valli
characters.role: Builder and sponsor of the show, the culprit
characters.personality: Loud, friendly on the surface, quick to blame others, proud of his company.
characters.purpose: The culprit: swapped the piece to keep his car park; tries to blame Aldo in Case 07; caught in Case 11.
characters.appearance: Fifties, big and broad, thick black eyebrows, a gold ring; a fine grey suit in town, a yellow helmet with a small crane sticker at his site.

relationships.relation: Ordered the plaster copy from her, saying the museum sent him.

characters.name: Aldo Rinaldi
characters.role: Professor of old maps, first a suspect, then a helper
characters.personality: Grumpy, impatient, deeply in love with old maps; generous once he trusts you.
characters.purpose: Act 1-2 red herring with a real alibi; Act 3's map expert (Latin words, the old street, Roman numbers).
characters.appearance: Seventies, small and thin, white beard, a green felt hat, ink-green fingers, a green notebook.

relationships.relation: Asked twice to see the piece early; she said no.
Buys plaster casts from her for his classes.

characters.name: Pia Ricci
characters.role: Flower seller at Campo de' Fiori
characters.personality: Cheerful, sharp-eyed, talks with her hands; forgets her own codes.
characters.purpose: Witness of Thursday night (the crane helmet, the heavy box, the dropped pass); breaks Valli's market story.
characters.appearance: Sixties, round and rosy, flowered apron, a red scarf on her hair.

relationships.relation: Kept Box 7 for 'the young woman with the owl ring'.

characters.name: Carla Bassi
characters.role: Plaster cast maker, owner of the Bassi workshop
characters.personality: Practical, proud of her craft, upset to learn she was used.
characters.purpose: Explains how a copy is made (the mould needs the real piece) and holds order 318.
characters.appearance: Forties, strong arms, rolled sleeves, a white-dusted apron, hair tied with a pencil; her orange cat Tito.

relationships.relation: Made his copy, told 'the museum sent him'.

locations.name: Capitoline Museums
locations.cityArea: Capitoline Hill, above the Roman Forum
locations.visual: Marble halls, tall windows, a glass case on a stand, an old guard room, a bright restoration lab.
locations.storyRole: Where the piece vanishes (Case 01), where Livia works (Case 08), where it returns (Case 12).

locations.name: Trevi Fountain
locations.cityArea: Trevi district, in narrow streets near the Quirinal
locations.visual: A huge baroque fountain of white stone, rushing water, stone shells along the basin, wide steps, coins in the water.
locations.storyRole: The Owl's second card, the professor's notebook, the marble tin.

locations.name: Campo de' Fiori
locations.visual: A morning market of flowers and lemons under white umbrellas; a flower stall with a red roof and numbered wooden boxes.
locations.storyRole: Box 7 and Pia's witness story (Case 03); Pia breaks Valli's market story at his office (Case 11).

locations.name: The Pantheon
locations.visual: A round temple with a great dome and an open eye of light; across the square, a tiny old bookshop.
locations.storyRole: The sunlight puzzle, the password and the plaster copy (Act 1's turn).

locations.name: Largo di Torre Argentina
locations.cityArea: A sunken square of Roman temples, between the Pantheon and the river
locations.visual: Ruined columns below street level, cats asleep on warm stones; nearby, a plaster workshop full of white statues.
locations.storyRole: Tito the cat and the Bassi workshop: who made the copy.

locations.name: Piazza Navona
locations.visual: A long oval square, the Fountain of the Four Rivers with its stone giants, painters and pigeons.
locations.storyRole: Aldo compared with the helmet man; the mirror word.

locations.name: University of Rome
locations.cityArea: Across the city, near the station
locations.visual: A lecture hall with wooden seats and a blackboard; a map archive of long flat drawers.
locations.storyRole: Aldo's alibi (Hall B) and his map cabinet with the city plan.

locations.name: The Spanish Steps
locations.visual: Wide stone steps rising to a twin-towered church, the boat fountain at the bottom, flower pots halfway up.
locations.storyRole: The chalk code, Valli's first lie, the loan book page.

locations.name: Tiber Island
locations.cityArea: In the river Tiber, between Trastevere and the old Jewish quarter
locations.visual: A boat-shaped island, the old Ponte Fabricio with its four-faced stone posts, plane trees, evening light on the water.

locations.name: The Roman Forum
locations.cityArea: Between the Capitoline and Palatine hills
locations.visual: Broken columns in long grass, a stone road, the arches of old temples, umbrella pines.
locations.storyRole: Reading the real piece's map: the library, the old street, the owl square.

locations.name: Piazza della Civetta
locations.cityArea: A small square at the end of the old market street (made up for the story)
locations.visual: A quiet square behind a tall site fence, a crane, a site office cabin; below it, a Roman library room with square holes and an owl mosaic.
locations.storyRole: Valli's building site, the real piece, the library saved.

acts.title: THE MISSING PIECE
acts.summary: The piece vanishes in ten dark minutes; the Owl's cards lead across Rome to a parcel.
acts.turningPoint: Case 04: the piece in the Owl's parcel is plaster. The Owl took a copy; the real piece was swapped earlier.

acts.title: THE COPY MAKER
acts.summary: From a cat's paw print to the copy's maker; the professor cleared; the sponsor lies; the Owl revealed.
acts.turningPoint: Case 08: the Owl is Livia. The swap was on Thursday night, and her drawing shows a room under Rome.

acts.title: UNDER THE OWL SQUARE
acts.summary: The map's library is under Piazza della Civetta, about to be buried; the real piece is found and Valli caught.
acts.turningPoint: Case 11: the real piece in Valli's box room, his lies broken, his plan told in order.

cases.title: The Empty Glass Case
cases.question: When did the piece go missing, and what was left?
cases.solution: In the ten dark minutes at midnight (two witnesses agree); the power stayed on, so the lights were turned off by hand; the Owl's card points to the fountain of wishes.
cases.toNext: The Owl's card: the fountain of wishes, the second shell.

cases.title: Under the Second Shell
cases.question: Where does the Owl's trail go, and who is the man in the green hat?
cases.solution: The riddle (a stone map), Aldo's wish (a suspect), the marble tin (key FIORI 7) and the route.
cases.fromPrevious: The Owl's card from the back door.

cases.title: Box 7 at the Flower Market
cases.question: What is in Box 7, and what did Pia see?
cases.solution: New white dust (a copy?); a big man in a crane helmet with a heavy box; his dropped museum pass.
cases.fromPrevious: Key FIORI 7 and the Owl's route.
cases.toNext: The roof with a round eye: the Pantheon.

cases.title: The Eye of the Pantheon
cases.question: What is in the Owl's parcel?
cases.solution: The book stone (two hours after the ship), the password FOUND, three tests: a plaster copy. The Owl took the copy out of the case.
cases.toNext: The copy's paw print and No. 3?8.

cases.title: The Cat Who Walked on the Copy
cases.question: Who made the copy, and for whom?
cases.solution: Tito the cat (orange, short tail, lives with plaster) leads to the Bassi workshop; order 318 was picked up by a man in a yellow helmet who had the real piece on Tuesday.
cases.fromPrevious: The paw print on the copy.
cases.toNext: Carla: the professor came on Tuesday too.

cases.title: The Professor's Alibi
cases.question: Did Professor Aldo take the piece?
cases.solution: No: small and thin, so not Pia's Thursday man; in Hall B at midnight on Friday. He saw a BUILDING box: the man is a builder.
cases.toNext: Aldo's photo of the real piece's crack.

cases.title: A Code on the Spanish Steps
cases.question: What does the Owl's code say, and is the sponsor honest?
cases.solution: TUESDAY; Valli's story about Aldo is false; the loan book: B.V. took the piece on Tuesday.
cases.fromPrevious: An owl card under Giulia's door.

cases.title: The Owl of Tiber Island
cases.question: Who is the Owl, and what happened that week?
cases.solution: The bridge with four-faced posts; Livia Conti is the Owl (her 'I worked late' of Case 01); the swap on Thursday night; her drawing of the real piece.

cases.title: The Street Under the Streets
cases.question: What is the room on the map, and where is it today?
cases.solution: A Roman library (the room with square holes for scrolls) under Piazza della Civetta, where Valli Building pours concrete on 10 May.
cases.toNext: The site at Piazza della Civetta.

cases.title: The Fence at Piazza della Civetta
cases.question: Whose site is it, and what came there on Thursday night?
cases.solution: The boss's helmet (yellow, with a crane) is B. Valli's; the heavy box came at 11:50 PM; Sofia calls the inspector.
cases.toNext: The site office with its light on.

cases.title: The Builder's Box Room
cases.question: Is the real piece in Valli's office, and can it be proved?
cases.solution: Stone C matches Aldo's photo; Pia and Sofia agree the market is closed on Sunday; the plan in order; the dropped pass makes him confess.
cases.toNext: The work stops; the square will be opened.

cases.title: The Library Under the Owl
cases.question: What is under the owl square?
cases.solution: The Roman library of the owl: scrolls, SAPIENTIA; seven gold tiles (found Y T, H O, S I R) spell HISTORY.

mysteryQuestions.question: When did the piece go missing?
mysteryQuestions.answer: In the ten dark minutes at midnight on Friday.

mysteryQuestions.question: Why does the Owl say the piece is not lost?
mysteryQuestions.answer: What the Owl took was a plaster copy.

mysteryQuestions.question: Is Professor Aldo the thief?
mysteryQuestions.answer: No: he was in Hall B at midnight, and he is not the big man.

mysteryQuestions.question: Who is the big man in the yellow helmet?
Who made the plaster copy?
mysteryQuestions.answer: Carla Bassi's workshop, order 318, for 'a museum friend'.

mysteryQuestions.question: When was the real piece swapped?
mysteryQuestions.answer: On Thursday night, when Valli came to 'check the lights'.

mysteryQuestions.question: Why would a builder want an old map?
mysteryQuestions.answer: It shows a Roman library under the square where he will pour concrete.

mysteryQuestions.question: Where is the real piece?
mysteryQuestions.answer: In the box room of Valli's site office.

mysteryQuestions.question: What is under Piazza della Civetta?
mysteryQuestions.answer: The Roman library of the owl.

clueThreads.meaning: Midnight on Friday: the time Aldo's alibi must cover, and Livia's 'I worked late in my lab' that gives the Owl away.
The white dust: soft, new, plaster — the copy's dust.
The first owl card: the same stamp, 'not lost', and the proof that Livia is the Owl.
Aldo's own page gives the hours the door log confirms.
The brass key opens Box 7.
FIORI 7: the box's number in Pia's code.
Pia's description clears the small, thin professor.
The crane helmet: a builder, then the boss's helmet at Valli's site, then the heavy box's night.
The pass Valli dropped on Thursday: the proof that makes him confess.
The plaster copy: its paw print, its number 3?8, and why Livia took it.
Tuesday at the workshop: what Aldo saw.
A mould needs the real piece: a link of Valli's plan.
The door log breaks Valli's story about Aldo.
Aldo's photo of the Y crack tells the real piece from the copies.
The crane on Valli's card matches the helmet.
The loan book page (Tuesday, B.V.) and the bridge card under it.
Livia's drawing: the half word, the street and its Roman-number stones.
Thursday night: the swap.
BIBLIOTHECA: a library, the word that stops the concrete.
The city plan: Valli Building's site, his motive, and the concrete that never came.
The heavy box nobody may open.
The real piece: the room it shows, and its return to the case.
Aldo's Latin card: Roman books were scrolls kept in square holes.

timeline.what: Valli borrows the piece from the lab 'for poster photos' (loan book, B.V.). At 3 PM, Carla makes a mould of it.
Valli picks up plaster copy 318 from the Bassi workshop.
Valli 'checks the lights' in the map hall (Enzo lets him in) and puts the copy in the glass case.
Pia sees a big man in a crane helmet with a heavy box; he drops his museum pass.
The heavy box comes through Valli's site gate at Piazza della Civetta.
Livia cleans the piece: too light, no crack. Sofia does not believe her.
Livia turns the lights off by hand, carries the copy out, leaves the owl card.
Enzo finds the case empty (Case 01); Trevi (Case 02); Pia's stall at 11:00 (Case 03); the Pantheon at noon (Case 04).
The owl square found, and Valli's site (Cases 09-10).
No concrete. The library is opened; the piece returns (Case 12).

notes: The witness talk asks three short questions; every answer is 4 to 8 words.
The Owl's card ('throw coins and make a wish') is matched to a picture of a girl throwing a coin, not to outside knowledge.
The riddle uses one pattern (I have X, but no Y) three times: easy to follow.
'Suspect' is in the glossary; Aldo's talk lines stay under 10 words.
Times with minutes (6:10 vs 6:30) are the main skill.
'Crane' is read from a definition list, so no word needs to be known before.
'Two hours after' is read on the guide sign, then found among four carved floor stones.
PLASTER is glossaried and contrasted with marble in the same letter.

englishReview.verdict: Fits; the round tag is still the trickiest reading step.
notes: Two cats are orange: 'short tail' and 'plaster workshop' must be read, so colour alone never answers.
'Mould' is British spelling, kept for the series' British voice; glossaried.

englishReview.verdict: Fits; PM/AM across midnight is new and taught by the hints.
notes: M1's notes no longer state the answer: the child compares Aldo with Pia's big man.
Reading GNIDLIUB backwards is a decoding skill, not vocabulary; hints give the method.

englishReview.verdict: Fits older players; the letter-shift code is Act 2's hardest puzzle.
notes: The code's rule is stated with three examples (B means A...).
Valli's story is short; the challenge is checking it against the Hall B log.
The bridge is chosen among three real bridges by 'two stone posts' and 'four faces'.
Livia's story is the longest speech of Act 2 (6 short lines); her talk lines are 4 to 9 words.

englishReview.verdict: Fits; Roman numbers with take-away (IV, IX) may need the second hint for 8-year-olds.
notes: The library is found in two steps: BIBLIO... in the Latin list, then 'square holes in the walls' in a picture.
'Between' and 'just before' carry the street puzzle.
The site rules pair a colour with a picture (yellow, with a crane): both must be read.
The final answer word LIBRARY was learned in Case 09.
'Monday to Saturday' and 'On Sunday, the square is empty' carry the talk: two agree, one does not.
The inspector's list mixes days and times: the hardest ordering of the season, with two hints.
WISDOM, WEALTH and WEATHER are given with definitions; the contrast carries the theme.
HISTORY is defined in the card ('the story of the past'); the tiles are listed out of order.
Written by Claude Code for the STEP 3-11 trial (input: Season 3, Rome). Not the decided Season 3.
Piazza della Civetta and its library are invented; Ponte Fabricio's four-faced posts, the Pantheon's oculus, Torre Argentina's cats and Campo de' Fiori's Monday-Saturday market are real.

STEP 3-14 (redesign for production): the core mystery, culprit, motive, characters, places and timeline are unchanged. Changed: how nine missions are played (two talks, four looks round, three picture choices), Case 06's two nights cleared in words, Case 11's Stone B (no second plaster copy), Case 12's tile order, and Livia's Case 01 answer paid off in Case 08.
